title: Clock skew, delayed fragment dedup, and visibility-latency: metering correctness investigation
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers and internal benchmarks have surfaced nondeterministic billing deltas tied to sessions that span multiple frontends and variable client clocks. Symptoms include: duplicated token counts when fragments arrive after visibility windows, undercounting when dedup markers are dropped, and quota hits reported late due to visibility-latency across the ingestion pipeline. This ticket scopes an investigation, design, and eventual fixes to make metering robust to clock skew, network reorder, and delayed fragments for multiplexed/streamed sessions.

Goals: (1) Define canonical per-session sequence semantics that tolerate out-of-order fragment arrival; (2) introduce idempotency/dedup rules for delayed fragments and markers; (3) quantify and eliminate cases where visibility-latency causes double or missed billing; (4) propose a rollout plan compatible with hosted and dedicated deployments.
proposed_solution:
Approach: 1) Add a session-level monotonic offset using server-assigned sequence tokens to replace client time as the primary ordering key. 2) Introduce a compact dedup token (sha256 of session-id + fragment-seq + fragment-curr-offset) attached to each fragment; ingestion will idempotently apply token counts only once. 3) Extend the visibility window semantics: a fragment is 'finalizable' only after both (a) server-seq > fragment-seq + safety-margin and (b) an optional explicit finalize marker is received. 4) For fragments arriving after finalize, run a reconciliation path that produces audit entries (no immediate billing change) and an async correction if needed. 5) Provide a compatibility shim that maps older clients to the new server-assigned sequence to avoid migration gaps.

Tradeoffs: server-assigned sequences add an extra hop but eliminate client clock reliance; dedup tokens increase metadata size but bound duplication risk. Async reconciliation avoids blocking foreground latency but complicates chargeback visibility for customers; we'll expose pending corrections in the Console until reconciled.
design_decisions:
- Primary ordering: server-assigned monotonic sequence (preferred) over client-supplied timestamps.
- Dedup strategy: store per-session 7-day Bloom-window plus deterministically stored sha256 tokens for terminal fragments.
- Reconciliation: non-blocking corrections published as 'billing adjustments' with audit trace and TTL.
- Backwards compatibility: accept client time for sessions < 2026-03-01 or when client flags legacy=true; otherwise require server-seq.
- Metrics: new metrics meter.reconciliations.count, meter.duplicate_attempts.count, meter.finalize_lag.ms.
- Opt-in toggles: feature flag 'server_seq_for_metering' rollable per-cluster.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit and integration tests that simulate: out-of-order fragments, duplicates, delayed finalize markers, and mid-session client clock jumps; token counts remain deterministic.
- End-to-end test showing no double-billing across frontends when fragments replayed.
- Graceful fallback: older clients continue to be billed correctly (no charge regressions) during rollout.
- New metrics show a decrease in duplicate_attempts and reconciliation volume by 90% in staging.
- Console shows pending adjustments for reconciliations and a visible audit trail.
- Change deployed behind feature flag; smoke tested on a small subset of customers with manual approval flow.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for sequence assignment, dedup-token generation, and dedup store eviction.
- Distributed integration test that replays recorded real-customer fragment traces with intentional clock skew and network reorder.
- Chaos test: simulate delayed fragment socket reconnects and server restarts to verify idempotence.
- Load test: measure added latency and metadata overhead at 99th percentile under realistic traffic shapes.
- Billing reconciliation dry-run: run reconciliation in read-only mode and compare results against legacy accounting for 72 hours.
- Telemetry validation: validate meter.reconciliations.count, meter.duplicate_attempts.count, and meter.finalize_lag.ms streams pipeline into Console dashboards.
- Rollback plan validated by a canary revert script to immediately disable 'server_seq_for_metering'.
risks:
- Increased per-fragment metadata may slightly impact throughput on high-traffic paths.
- If reconciliation logic has bugs, customers may see confusing pending adjustments.
- Cross-cluster session routing may complicate a single authoritative sequence assignment; requires a deterministic leader or consistent hashing.
- Bloom-window false positives could hide duplicate attempts; design must prefer correctness over small overstorage.
- Coordination with Dedicated/Private install teams to ensure feature-flag propagation and KMS/noise considerations.
rollout_plan:
1) Implement feature behind 'server_seq_for_metering' and unit tests. 2) Deploy to staging and run dry-run reconciliation for 72 hours. 3) Canary deploy to 2% of production traffic (non-enterprise customers) for 7 days; monitor metrics and billing adjustments. 4) Expand to 25% and then 100% by customer cohorts, offering opt-out for enterprise customers during transition windows. 5) After 30 days at 100%, enable async corrections (automatic adjustments). 6) Deprecate legacy client time window after 90 days.

Communication: post runbook and migration notes in Confluence and send patch notes to SRE and Customer Success teams prior to each phase.
implementation_notes:
- Add new server_seq generator in frontend gateway; generator must be idempotent for retried accepts.
- Dedup-store: write-once append-only index keyed by session+sha256 token with TTL 7d. Use existing redis-cluster with 2x sharding for high volume.
- Reconciliation worker will be implemented as a separate service that consumes 'late-fragment' events and writes adjustments to billing ledger via the existing ledger API.
- Console changes: show 'pending adjustments' and link to audit trace; add a filter for reconciliations.
